messages:
lucy: headsup — since ~21:40 UTC we're seeing elevated 502/504s from the hosted API edge for a subset of tenants, started right after the auth-cache deploy. customer impact: realtime chat streams failing (timeouts). sample curl: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' --data @payload.json` returns `502` with `upstream reset`

michael: thanks lucy. can you paste one `trace_id` from a failing request and the `edge` response headers? also which region?

lucy: trace_id: `tr-0a1b2c3d`. region: us-west-2. edge headers: `server: envoy`, `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 0`, `x-request-id: tr-0a1b2c3d`. attaching small log snippet: ```
[21:40:12] edge: conn reset to upstream auth-proxy (10.1.5.23:8443) trace=tr-0a1b2c3d
[21:40:12] auth-proxy: 503 downstream error, cache-miss spike
```

deploy-bot: deployment `auth-cache:v2026.03.18-21` completed at 2026-03-18T21:37:45Z to us-west-2

sara: escalated to priority-high and opened ticket CS-4532 (customer flagged 20% error rate for one tenant). @kevin can you join? :eyes:

kevin: on it. quick question — do we have a repro for the failing call without customer data? lucy: can you try the same curl but with `X-Debug-Traces: true` and a small payload?

lucy: repro steps minimal: small POST body, replicate 10x parallel. i ran: `seq 1 10 | xargs -P10 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"hi"}'` -> results: 6x 200, 4x 502 (timeouts ~0.4s)

ivan: looking at metrics — auth-cache saw a TTL expiry storm after deploy, backend auth-service took longer to respond; backend returned 500 intermittently which caused upstream to reset. suspicion: cache warmup race + h2 stream window limits on edge -> connection churn.

michael: possible mitigations: 1) revert auth-cache deploy (safe but disruptive) 2) increase edge upstream timeout & enable retry/failover to fallback auth replica 3) restart auth-cache pods one at a time to warm caches gradually

ashley: customers impacted are on trial plans; CS wants an ETA before we rollback. what's least risky and fastest?

kevin: fastest safe: bump upstream timeout to 5s and enable a single retry to fallback auth (edge config override), then serial restart of cache pods. I'll run the config change now if eng approves. :thumbsup:

ivan: I'll push a canary config to us-west-2 with increased timeouts + `retry_on: 5xx` for auth upstream and monitor for 5m. if success, roll to all. Also suggest reducing h2 concurrent streams per connection to avoid RST storms.

michael: agree. note to ops: set circuit-breaker thresholds higher temporarily. I'll supervise.

lucy: applied quick repro after edge timeout bump — re-run 10-parallel test: 9x 200, 1x 502. much better. attaching new trace tr-0a1b2c9d (success).

sara: updating CS-4532 with mitigation steps and ETA. informing customer: temporary config change applied, follow-up full rollback if needed.

kevin: keeping an eye on error-rate dashboards and logs. if errors climb back above 5% we'll revert to full rollback. thanks everyone. :pray:

michael: follow-ups: (1) postmortem once stable, (2) add cache-warmup job before deploy, (3) add an automated canary that simulates warmup on deploy.

lucy: noted. i'll capture repro script and upload to the incident doc. end thread.
